reuse.why: Builds on the existing WeekendRule/applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay abstraction and getDateWithSkippedWeekend, extending them with frequency and holidays rather than adding parallel helpers.

duplication.why: The 'drop off-days for daily schedules, then apply the weekend rule' step is re-written in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and the WeekendRule object is assembled by hand at each site (twice inside getNextDate).

placement.why: Rules (isOffDay, skipsWeekendOccurrences, holiday shifting) sit in shared/schedules.ts; the range handler sits with getUpcomingDates in schedules/app.ts, though its window constant is local to the handler.

scope.why: Limited to schedule date logic, its callers, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared rule is coherent, but 'whether to skip' is decided inside applyWeekendRule while 'dropping' is left to each caller, and schedule-template must pass an inverted keepWeekends flag to getNextDate, so the split is easy to get wrong.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and getNextDate each filter daily off-days themselves with isOffDay instead of the WeekendRule abstraction owning the drop step.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange reshapes getUpcomingDates' occurrence loop (filter off-days, applyWeekendRule, dayFromDate) with a widened window and a set; getNextDate expresses the same filter as an isKept predicate.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains frequency and holidays; applyWeekendRule and applyWeekendRuleToDay gain a '!skipsWeekendOccurrences' daily special case; getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange re-implement the daily drop outside the abstraction.
